lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Suggest a more sustainable swap for single-use plastic wrapping on a school model and one trade-off.

FEEDBACK
e.g. paper/tape or reused container; trade-off may be water resistance/strength.

WATCH FOR
Calling a design green while using excess new materials each trial ignores waste.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Audit your project materials. Replace two items with reused options if safe. Write a short impact paragraph.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Audit your project materials. Replace two items with reused options if safe. Write a short impact paragraph. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new object/context, two named observations, claim about sustainable linked to that evidence.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Calling a design green while using excess new materials each trial ignores waste.. Correction: e.g. paper/tape or reused container; with evidence.

Parent: Likely misconception: Calling a design green while using excess new materials each trial ignores waste. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses sustainable. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about sustainable, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept a new example with named observations and a claim–evidence link about sustainable. Reject title-only labels with no observation. / Accept a misconception plus corrected claim and evidence reason for sustainable. Reject wording changes that leave the same error..

teach_steps.explain:
Sustainable design choices prefer reusable/recycled materials, less waste and designs that last or repair easily when suitable.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Calling a design green while using excess new materials each trial ignores waste. Correct the claim or method, not just the neatness of the diagram.
